items.title: What Would A Stalled MAX Line Do To Boeing Stock?
items.summary: Boeing (BA) has been lifting 737 MAX output to 47 jets a month. On September 16, its chief executive said steadying that pace was taking longer than expected. The 737 MAX program serves as Boeing’s primary commercial cash driver, making line stability essential to meeting company-wide cash flow targets. If the MAX line cannot steady at 47 a month, what does that mean for Boeing’s financial recovery and stock valuation.

items.title: Is GE Aerospace Giving Up Margin for Growth?
items.summary: GE Aerospace (GE) holders should watch one number: the profit margin of its commercial engine business. Profit margin is the share of sales kept as profit. That margin fell to 27.3% in the second quarter of 2026 from 28.9% a year earlier. This unit made $2.7 billion in profit that quarter, about the same amount as the company's total operating profit. Should a holder worry that this margin is slipping as GE Aerospace grows.

items.title: North Korea tests swarm attacks combining drones and missiles - WSJ
items.summary: Investing.com -- North Korea has begun testing swarm attacks combining drones, missiles, rockets and artillery, adopting tactics used in Ukraine and the Middle East that could put greater pressure on U.S. and allied air defences, the Wall Street Journal reported.

items.title: U.S. understands Taiwan’s defence needs amid China threat, official says
items.summary: Investing.com -- The United States understands Taiwan’s defence requirements and the military pressure it faces from China, a senior Taiwanese diplomat said Sunday following last week’s summit between U.S. and Chinese leaders, Reuters reported.

items.title: Northrop Grumman (NOC) Lands Navy Radar Deal On Undervalued Stock Narrative
items.summary: Northrop Grumman (NOC) has secured a US$123.8 million contract from the U.S. Navy to produce 67 APG-85 radars for the F-35 program, providing production visibility through February 2031. The contract lands at a time when Northrop Grumman’s 1-year total shareholder return is down 12.7%, while the 3-year and 5-year total shareholder returns of 21.9% and 53.4% point to a stronger long-run record and indicate that recent momentum has faded.
